title: The Living Measure
author: Ethan James Farrell
description: A custom work of cosmological fiction from Ethan's collection (2026), opening with the line 'Before the first name, there was a Person shaped like everything.' Written in a lyrical, mythopoeic voice and framed with invented scripture such as 'the lost hymn of the Gatherers', it dramatises a creation myth in which the Infinite withdraws to make room and the first thing to enter that space is a cosmic Face containing the map of every face that will ever wake. The story draws imaginatively on the Lurianic themes of contraction, the primordial human of light, fragmentation and restoration, and on the Gnostic Anthropos, turning the ideas explored in the library's non-fiction studies of Adam Kadmon into narrative. It should be read as fiction inspired by esoteric cosmology, not as a historical or scriptural source.
editionNote: Curator-supplied PDF and EPUB from the organised ebook collection. One format was converted from the other (EPUB from PDF).
